title: PrincipalErased
description:
`principal_erased` — the ONE admin event of a completed erasure (erasure spec D1).

ONE TYPE for identity erasure and content erasure: the distinction rides the per-target
outcomes as data, never the type boundary — two types would cost the pairing (one request,
one operator, one reference) and double registration for no additional guarantee. The
subject is the PSEUDONYM the act itself broke; the event never re-identifies — no name, no
email, no case description. The request reference does not ride here: it lives on
`kb_events."references"`, the apparatus this act owns.

The redacted set is keyed on CONTENT HASH (D2) — never row ids, which would collide with
the trail functions' join-key shapes. The erased-content set (D4) rebuilds from these
payloads alone.

actor.description:
The acting operator, distinguishable from the subject — self-serve vs administrative
is a comparison the auditor needs. `None` only where no actor exists to name; inventing
one would put a fabricated attribution on the ledger (the standing-event precedent).

charters_held.description: The estate's charters, emptied and held until map-grain erasure (D3).

estate_contexts.description:
The estate the act reached (20261021100000, person-erasure design D1): the subject's @me
contexts and their personal team's contexts, in id order. The redaction reads it back from
here, so replay reaches the set live reached. Required, and written even when empty: the
redaction raises without it, and no `principal_erased` predates it (the migration guards).

redacted_fields.description:
The estate contexts' ledger copies of their names and slugs this act rewrote to the
sentinels (20261022100000, R7): `context_renamed`, `context_retired` and
`context_restored` paths, in the shape `resource_erased` uses. Paths only, never values.
Required, and written even when empty: no `principal_erased` predates it (the migration
guards).

redacted_hashes.description:
The redacted set (D2): bare sha256 hex, exactly as `content_hash` carries it — the key
every reader already shares and no trail join-key shape can match.

resource_erasures.description: The resource erasures the act ran over the estate, in the order it ran them (D4).

retained.description:
The categories the deployment's retention policy kept (20261023100000, R4), as the policy
stood when the act ran. The redaction reads them back from here, as it reads the estate, so
replay keeps what live kept. Required, and written even when empty: no `principal_erased`
predates it (the migration guards).

subject_id.description: The pseudonym — `kb_profiles.id`. It survives; its identifying power does not (D5).

targets.description:
Per-target outcomes and the named remainder (D6's accepted-in-part arm): anything
unhonourable is named here. Partial completion is data, never a silent success.

AnchorTable.description: A polymorphic anchor/endpoint reference. Serializes table names exactly as the DDL spells them.

ErasureTargetOutcome.description:
One target of a completed erasure and what happened to it (erasure spec, "per-target
outcomes"). The target names itself the way the personal-data manifest does — `table` or
`table.column`; the outcome is the act's own record of what redaction applied. Deliberately
open-textured in v1: ceilings are DATA, not types (D1), and the per-target vocabulary is the
execution build's to pin. `unhonourable_scope` outcomes land here, never silent.

outcome.description: What the act did to it (erased / sentinel-scrubbed / accepted-in-part / …).

EstateResourceErasureKind.description: Whether that resource erasure was a first erasure or a completion pass (D2's `complete`).

EstateResourceErasureRef.description:
One resource erasure a person act ran: its subject and its `resource_erased` event. Keyed
`resource` and `event`, never `resource_id`: the completion payload carries no key the trail
functions join on.

RedactedEventFields.description:
The ledger paths of one event: redacted (`redacted_fields`) or named-and-unreached
(`ledger_remainder`). ONE shape for both, so the cut-2 completion pass derives what it redacts
from what cut 1 recorded without translating (resource erasure spec D12). The event is keyed
`event`, never `event_id` — no trail join-key shape rides an admin payload (D1). Paths only,
never values: the record of a redaction must not carry what was redacted.

paths.description: JSON paths within that event's `payload` (or `metadata`), e.g. `title`, `origin_uri`.

RetainedCategory.description:
One category a person erasure kept under the deployment's retention policy, as the act's record
carries it: the policy as it stood when the act ran, so the record stays true after the policy
changes and replay keeps exactly what the live act kept.

period.description: The stated period, as Postgres renders the interval (`1 year`).

RetentionCategory.description:
What a deployment's retention policy may keep through a person erasure (R4 of the 2026-10-10
erasure inventory). The act removes every identifier of the subject and every free-text field
about them by default; a category here is kept only when an organisation names it in a policy
with a stated basis and period, and the record then names it `retained under policy <name>`.

Free text and replay evidence only. Identifiers and live credentials are not retainable: a
deployment cannot keep a usable credential or a direct identifier of an erased person, so no
value here names one. The SQL CHECK on `kb_erasure_retention_policies.category` is the same
closed set.

oneOf.description:
`kb_oauth_refresh_replays`: the evidence that one of the subject's refresh tokens was
copied. Kept with its tokens, which stay revoked with their claims and hash erased.
